findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offset
findings.body: In the new isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut) matcher, matchesSafely does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two bugs: (1) the condition is inverted — the matcher returns false exactly when the grant shortcut equals the expected one, and returns true (if the rest is a UUID) when it does NOT match; (2) the offset is wrong — in a token id like `onrtac:<uuid>` the 2-char grant shortcut occupies positions 4-5, so it should be substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5) (which yields e.g. "ta"). The correct check would be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. As written, every event assertion switched to this matcher (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) will fail against correctly-encoded token ids, breaking a large part of the integration test suite.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant type providers
findings.body: getShortcut() is added as a new abstract method with no default implementation on the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface. Any existing custom OAuth2 grant type provider (compiled against the previous interface) will fail with AbstractMethodError at runtime — and it will be hit during server startup, because DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() unconditionally calls gtf.getShortcut() on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. A default method (e.g. returning null, or a shortcut derived from getId()) combined with null-handling in the encoder factory would keep backward compatibility for third-party grant providers.

findings.title: Grant type only recorded for standard token exchange, not other exchange flows
findings.body: The Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute is set to the token-exchange grant type only inside StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient. Other token exchange providers built on AbstractTokenExchangeProvider (the legacy V1 token exchange behind the TOKEN_EXCHANGE feature, subject impersonation V2, federated exchange) never set this attribute, so access tokens minted through those flows will encode the grant type as "na" (unknown) even though they went through the token-exchange grant. Since recognizing the token-exchange grant is one of the stated goals of this PR (issue #37117), the attribute should be set in a shared place (e.g. TokenExchangeGrantType.process or AbstractTokenExchangeProvider) so all exchange variants are covered.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — a copy-paste of the line above. It checks grantType a second time (with a misleading message about rawTokenId) and never null-checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId then silently propagates and would be rendered as the literal string "null" by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId when concatenating the token id. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: getShortcut() javadoc contradicts the mandatory 2-character format
findings.body: The javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId strictly requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 characters (2 per segment) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise, and the whole PR design assumes every shortcut is exactly 2 characters. A grant factory returning a 3-letter shortcut (as the javadoc suggests) would produce token ids that can never be decoded. The javadoc should state that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and unique, and ideally postInit should validate the length.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason (NPE from null sessionFactory)
findings.body: In testIncorrectGrantType, the factory's postInit() is never called, so its sessionFactory field is null. Decoding "ofrtac:5678" reaches DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"), which — not finding the shortcut in the manually populated map — calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) and throws a NullPointerException. The test catches plain RuntimeException, so it passes on the NPE rather than on the intended IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type"). The test should assert the specific exception type/message (and ideally initialize the factory via postInit with a real or mocked session factory) so it actually verifies the unknown-shortcut handling.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from grant SPI class
findings.body: The diff removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context). Nothing in the repository uses it anymore, but Context is a public static class of the OAuth2 grant type SPI, so any external custom grant implementation that built a derived context via this constructor will fail to compile or link after upgrade. Since the field set is otherwise identical, keeping the constructor (now also copying grantType) would avoid an unnecessary compatibility break for custom providers.
